definition: Incremental means increasing or developing little by little, in small, regular steps.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word incremental. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know incremental should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The company's price increases were incremental, so small each month that customers barely noticed them add up.

A gardener who waters her seedlings sporadically — a splash whenever she happens to remember — watches them struggle, because sporadic effort lacks the regular, accumulating rhythm that makes improvement incremental.

Saying a glacier melted gradually tells us only that the change was slow; calling a reading habit incremental tells us more — progress arrives in small, countable steps, like one extra page added every night.

Piecemeal means done a piece at a time, with no master plan — repairs made piecemeal happen whenever something breaks. Incremental also moves in small steps, but the steps are regular and add up by design. A piecemeal renovation is patchwork; an incremental one follows a schedule of small, planned stages.

Progressive means moving forward, with each stage carrying the process further, but it says nothing about step size. Incremental insists the advance comes in small, measured steps. A progressive rollout might leap from ten users to ten thousand; an incremental one adds a hundred at a time.

Continuous means unbroken and flowing, with no pauses or seams at all. Incremental is the opposite texture: progress arrives in distinct little steps you could count. A dimmer that slides smoothly is continuous; one that clicks through ten brightness settings is incremental.

Incremental means increasing or developing little by little, in small, regular steps.
The engineer improved the software in incremental steps, fixing one small bug per week, and after fifty weeks, the performance had nearly doubled.
Incremental means not just small changes, but small regular steps that add up over time.
The engineer's weekly bug fixes are a perfect example: each fix is tiny, but the regularity and accumulation over fifty weeks created a major improvement.
That precision — 'small, repeated steps that compound' — is exactly what incremental names.
Incremental is a business and science word for steady, small-step improvements.
In everyday speech, say 'gradual' or 'little by little.' Use incremental when emphasizing that progress comes through repeated small additions, not sudden jumps.

After the near-miss flood, the city rejected the grand plan for a new levee as unaffordable and adopted an incremental one instead.
Each budget year would add exactly eighteen inches of height along one numbered section, in a published order, until the whole ring stood six feet taller.
Critics jeered that eighteen inches was nothing against a river.
The engineers agreed — and pointed out that the schedule never missed a year, while grand plans had been voted down four times in a generation.
Twelve years later the ring was finished.
The river obliged with its worst spring on record, and the water stopped eleven inches below the new crown.
